newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria president vetoes deposit guarantee law.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria president vetoes deposit guarantee law.

text.p: Bulgaria's president Zhelyu Zhelev on Friday vetoed amendments to a deposit guarantee law delaying compensation payments for personal and company deposits in bankrupt banks, the official news agency BTA said.
"Once more Bulgarian citizens are being fed unrealistic promises," said Zhelev in a statement explaining his veto.

Under amendments passed by parliament two weeks ago, citizens' lev deposits in insolvent banks would be fully repaid by the state no sooner than 30 days after the court declares the banks insolvent and companies would be able to draw their lev deposits from insolvent banks 60 days after the ruling.
So far compensation payments have begun immediately after the central bank filed an insolvency suit to the courts.
The new amendments block personal and company accounts for an indefinite period of time, violating the legal rights of depositors to access their funds, said Zhelev in the statement published by BTA.
This may cause insolvencies of smaller companies which have several hundred thousand levs or dollars blocked in these banks, the statement said.
"The amendments create a legal uncertainty which continues to erode confidence in banks," said the statement.
The law provided for a 100 percent state guarantee on personal savings in bankrupt banks and 50 percent coverage of companies' deposits.

Under the new amendments, personal foreign exchange deposits in bankrupt banks will be compensated in four semi-annual tranches, but the first instalment will be paid six months after the court rules on those banks' insolvency.

Under the law, the government issued treasury bonds worth a total of 80 billion levs and $100 million, which were placed with the State Savings Bank and the state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank to guarantee payments to depositors in the five banks.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has filed insolvency suits against five local banks since May in line with bank stabilisation pledges made to multilteral lenders.
The BNB placed a further nine banks in receivership last month aiming to evaluate their financial state and then decide for which of them to seek insolvency.

"Confidence in the banks can be restored only with a clear programme based on the real financial situation and not with half measures which constantly change to meet unrealistic promises," said the statement.
Parliament now can either accept Zhelev's comments and alter the law, or overturn the veto and pass the law at a second reading.
